Then, we injected AV with AAV1-CamKIIa-hChR2-mCherry to anterogradely label TC axons, which indicated that in mice these axons indeed target primarily L1 in RSCg, and particularly L1a (its outermost sublayer), with additional sparser branching in deeper layers and in dysgranular RSC (Fig. 3b). To further assess if these L1 axons in RSCg arise from AV neurons, which may branch in other layers (Odagiri et al., 2011) , and/or from TC neurons in surrounding nuclei such as the anterodorsal nucleus 17,(Shibata, 1993) , we repeated this experiment using Grp_KH288-Cre mice, a driver line showing Cre-expressing neurons in a subset of AV nucleus neurons but none in the anterodorsal nucleus (Supplementary Fig. S6a-h). Following injection of AV with Cre-dependent AAV5-Ef1a-DIO-hChR2-EYFP, we again observed labeled axons in L1 (Fig. 3c,d and Supplementary Fig. S6i-m), supporting the results obtained with wild-type mice indicating that AV, rather than the anterodorsal nucleus, is the main source of L1targeting projections from the ATN to the RSCg.
